rulings.challenge_claim: The row leans on a ketiv/qere-bearing verse for its internal mark disclosure without any apparatus disclosure, and rests its closing device on a divine title whose Hebrew object it never names - one the English rendering flattens into the same words as the different stack quoted at the neighbouring seam.
rulings.grounds: Byte-re-derived; both prongs are real but both need reframing, so refine. PRONG 1 (ketiv/qere): the site is real — MT 10:32 carries one note, staged as the doubled pair inside הַ֣ר בית בַּת צִיּ֔וֹן (web:Isa.10.32, byte tier for the spliced run; the ketiv member is unpointed and is skeleton grade standing alone) — and this row is the strongest of the five such cases in these clusters, because it does not merely contain the verse: it lists web:Isa.10.32 in its own evidence refs and argues from that verse's paragraph mark, engaging the verse while passing over its apparatus. CORPUS EVIDENCE I DERIVED FOR THIS RULING (and which corrects my own earlier framing of this class): across the whole frozen corpus, 43 rows have a ketiv/qere verse inside their span; 35 of them disclose it and 8 do not. Five of those eight sit in these two clusters, and this writer part discloses in only 1 of its 5 such rows, while a sibling part carries the attested formulation for exactly this case — a reference entry reading 'ketiv/qere note, single-witness; content not sliced'. So disclosure of an in-span ketiv/qere verse is settled corpus PRACTICE at a 35-of-43 rate, not merely one part's habit. It is still NOT a Tier-0 debt: the mark-check's unconditional span-relevant symmetry sweep covers petuchah and setumah only, its ketiv/qere arm validates claims that are made, and this row passes every Tier-0 check clean. The primaries reach the right conclusion by the wrong rationale — nothing is 'owed before slicing', because no slicing occurs; what is real is a documented practice deviation. PRONG 2 (divine title): the byte facts verify but the framing overstates. The row does not rest its closing device on a title — its device is the presentative formula, and it splices the Hebrew הִנֵּ֤ה הָאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.33, byte tier) at byte tier, rendered “Behold, the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, will lop the boughs with terror. The tall will be cut down, and the lofty will be brought low.” (web:Isa.10.33). What is real is narrower: the title inside that quoted run is the definite-article stack, a count-object reaching 5 verses at skeleton tier (MT 1:24, 3:1, 10:16, 10:33, 19:4), and it is a DIFFERENT object from אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.24, byte tier; 8 verses at skeleton, and exactly 2 at byte tier) standing at the seam of neighbouring rows — yet both render identically in English, and the row names no title object and carries no divine-title signal key beyond the presentative. The in-chapter recurrence at הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.16, byte tier) is identical to the closing stack at accent-stripped and skeleton tier but NOT at byte tier, and it sits two rows away rather than across this row's own seam, so the cross-seam cohesion rule does not trigger — it is a recurrence to name, not a straddling device. WHAT VERIFIES AND IS NOT CONTESTED: the march onset splice; both parashah claims under the correct type (setumah at MT 10:32 inside the span and setumah at MT 10:34 at its close, tier-3, single witness, no petuchah in the span); treating the place-name sequence as enumeration inside the unit rather than as a list register; and — the row's real strength — disclosing the internal presentative seam candidate AND giving an argued reason to hold the unit across it. SEVERITY: lowered to low. Nothing here is byte-false and no device straddles this row's seam; both prongs are disclosure-register gaps against a seam argument that otherwise verifies.
rulings.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field boundary_evidence_refs or device_notes: disclose the in-span ketiv/qere note at web:Isa.10.32, using the formulation already attested elsewhere in the corpus for a verse whose letter bytes the row does not slice. Field device_notes: name the divine-title count-object carried inside the quoted presentative run at web:Isa.10.33 — the definite-article stack, distinguishing it from the differently-formed stack standing at web:Isa.10.24 that the English renders identically — and give its tier and digit (5 verses at skeleton tier). Field observed_substrate_signals: keep the presentative key and add a divine_title.* key naming the stack rather than the formula. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: every divine-name engagement names WHICH count-object it engages before any digit, and no title claim rests on an English rendering that flattens two distinct Hebrew stacks; the mark and ref checks stay clean and the existing internal-seam disclosure is preserved intact.

rulings.challenge_claim: The cut itself is well founded on the bytes, but both structural claims the row offers as its grounds - the stump image answering the felled trees across its front seam, and the closing inclusio - are asserted with no quoted Hebrew form and no tier label, and neither has a byte-level anchor.
rulings.grounds: Byte-re-derived; the challenge verifies as stated and is upheld. The cut itself is sound and not contested: the onset splice וְיָצָ֥א חֹ֖טֶר מִגֵּ֣זַע יִשָׁ֑י (oshb:Isa.11.1, byte tier) matches the source bytes and enters a fresh grammatical subject, “A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit.” (web:Isa.11.1); the mark layer is right (setumah at MT 10:34, petuchah at MT 11:9, correct types, none inside MT 11:1-11:8, and no ketiv/qere note anywhere in the span, so nothing is owed there). What fails is that both structural claims the row offers as grounds are asserted with no quoted Hebrew form, no tier label and no lexical anchor. FRONT-SEAM CLAIM: the three growth nouns of the onset verse — חֹ֖טֶר (oshb:Isa.11.1, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse), מִגֵּ֣זַע (oshb:Isa.11.1, byte tier; sweep: 2 verses, MT 11:1 and 40:24) and וְנֵ֖צֶר (oshb:Isa.11.1, byte tier; sweep: 5 verses), the sweeps all at skeleton tier — share no root with the felling vocabulary of MT 10:33-10:34, so the claim that the stump image 'answers' the felled trees is a semantic reading with no byte-level anchor on either side; I independently re-swept all three digits and they hold on the objects named. CLOSING CLAIM: the 'inclusio' names no bracketing term, quotes no form and labels no tier, and the nearest candidate fails — MT 11:9's דֵּעָה֙ (oshb:Isa.11.9, byte tier; that skeleton reaches 8 verses) is not the form attested at MT 11:2, ר֥וּחַ דַּ֖עַת (oshb:Isa.11.2, byte tier; the bare knowledge-noun there reaches 26 verses at skeleton), so no bracket closes at any Hebrew tier. ONE FRAMING NOTE, not adopted and not needed for the defect: the challenge's evidence adds that a semantic continuity across the row's own seam argues against the cut rather than for it. That inference is available but optional — the row can equally be read as disclosing a cross-seam echo, which is the right register; the defect stands either way, because on either reading the claim carries no form and no tier. The back seam is sounder and the challenge says so: the figure does continue into the next verse, מִשָּׁרָשָׁ֥יו (oshb:Isa.11.1, byte tier) answered by שֹׁ֣רֶשׁ יִשַׁ֗י (oshb:Isa.11.10, byte tier). Severity low is right: the cut holds; the grounds under it are under-evidenced.
rulings.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field boundary_rationale: either splice the felling vocabulary from MT 10:33-10:34 beside the growth nouns of web:Isa.11.1 and state the tier at which the two relate — naming it as a semantic, not lexical, echo, since the roots do not meet at skeleton tier — or drop the 'answers the felled trees' sentence and rest the front seam on the fresh grammatical subject, which the bytes already carry unaided. Field boundary_rationale: replace the bare word 'inclusio' either with the bracketing TERM, quoted at both ends with its tier named, or with a plainer closure claim; the knowledge-nouns at web:Isa.11.2 and web:Isa.11.9 are different forms and do not bracket at any Hebrew tier, so they cannot be the unnamed bracket. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): every structural label that names a device — inclusio, echo, bracket — carries a quoted form at each end plus the tier at which the two match, and no boundary-relevant claim stands on an English-only reading; the mark and ref checks stay clean.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: the one-verse cut rests on an in-that-day formula that the immediately following verse repeats verse-initially at accent-stripped and skeleton tier, and on a second-time marker that is not that verse's opener, with a two-site banner catchword straddling the same seam undisclosed; also, calling one paragraph-break type the more emphatic of the two is a scribal-convention assertion not sourced from the inventory cited. LF: the named rejected alternative is not clearly the strongest rival, since the verse's own nations/ensign scope continues the preceding unit at least as strongly as it anticipates the regathering oracle, and the coda reading the row's own device notes concede is never adjudicated in that field.
rulings.grounds: Both primaries hit this row with DISTINCT defects; the core is real but two of the four supports mis-attach and the severity is too high, so refine. UPHELD CORE: the row's sole onset driver recurs verse-initially at the very next verse. MT 11:10 opens וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.11.10, byte tier) and MT 11:11 opens וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier); I re-derived the tiers directly and confirm they are identical at accent-stripped AND skeleton tier and differ ONLY in accents, so not byte-identical — a tier the row names nowhere. The formula reaches 13 verses at skeleton tier, four of them in this immediate stretch. A driver that both sides of a seam carry cannot by itself mark the seam, and the row neither discloses the recurrence nor labels its tier. ALSO UPHELD, and the cleanest defect here: the row calls one paragraph-break type 'the more emphatic of the two'. That is a scribal-convention ranking sourced from nothing — the single-witness inventory the row cites records type and count only, and the governing addendum requires petuchah and setumah never be conflated while granting no ranking between them. MIS-ATTACHED SUPPORT 1: 'a second-time marker that is not that verse's opener' is a true byte fact — שֵׁנִית֙ (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier) is the sixth token of MT 11:11 — but the DEFECT it names belongs to the sibling row, which presents that run as what opens its unit; THIS row never claims the marker opens the verse, only that it distinguishes the two actions. Against this row the point survives only in a weaker form: the distinguishing token sits after the shared frame, so it cannot carry the seam weight assigned to it. MIS-ATTACHED SUPPORT 2: the banner straddle is real — עֹמֵד֙ לְנֵ֣ס עַמִּ֔ים (oshb:Isa.11.10, byte tier) and וְנָשָׂ֥א נֵס֙ לַגּוֹיִ֔ם (oshb:Isa.11.12, byte tier) — but the cited two-verse digit belongs to the MT 5:26 and 11:12 pairing, a different object from the 11:10-to-11:12 straddle it is adduced for. On my own sweeps the straddling collocations are 1 verse and 2 verses at skeleton tier respectively, and the bare banner noun is a short-token trap matching 44 verses of mostly unrelated forms — so the straddle must be argued from the attested collocations, never from the bare noun. LF's DISTINCT ITEM, upheld: the formal rejected-alternative field names only the forward fold into the regathering oracle, while the row's own device_notes concedes three readings including the coda reading; the field that must carry the strongest rival never adjudicates the rival the row itself concedes. VERIFIES: both petuchah claims under the correct type (MT 11:9 and MT 11:10), rightly declined as drivers; no ketiv/qere in the span; and the honest medium_low hold with the frontier flag set. SEVERITY: lowered from high to medium — the surviving core is squarely medium, but two supports mis-attach, the row already carries its uncertainty in the right band with the flag set, and every Tier-0 check is clean.
rulings.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field device_notes: delete the phrase ranking one paragraph-break type as more emphatic than the other — no such ranking is sourceable from the single-witness inventory; keep the type names distinct and unranked. Field boundary_rationale or device_notes: disclose that the in-that-day formula opening this verse also opens the immediately following verse, naming the tier explicitly (identical at accent-stripped and skeleton tier, NOT byte) and the digit (13 verses at skeleton tier), and state what is left carrying the seam once a frame shared by both sides is set aside. Field device_notes: disclose the banner recurrence across the back seam from web:Isa.11.10 to web:Isa.11.12 using the attested collocations with their own digits and tier — never the bare banner noun, whose skeleton is a short-token trap. Field strongest_rejected_alternative: replace or extend it so the rival actually adjudicated is the strongest one the row concedes elsewhere, namely reading this verse as the closing coda of the preceding unit. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: no formula may drive a cut without a disclosed tier and a stated reason it discriminates the seam it draws; every recurrence digit names the object it counts; and the rejected-alternative field carries the rival the row's own notes concede. BOUNDARY NOTE: whether this one-verse unit should stand, fold back, or fold forward is a boundary question reserved to the boss — I considered escalating it and did not, because the defects ruled here are evidence-layer and the row already holds the boundary at medium_low with the rival disclosed. Nothing in this remedy authorises a respan.

rulings.challenge_claim: The run presented as what opens the unit is mid-verse, while the verse's actual opener is the same formula carrying the boundary at MT 11:10, and the row names only one of the two remnant-root objects that are live in the two verses it cites.
rulings.grounds: Byte-re-derived; two prongs verify squarely and the challenge is upheld. PRONG 1 (the run presented as the opener is mid-verse): verified and material. The row states that the second-time marker opens the unit and splices יוֹסִ֨יף אֲדֹנָ֤י שֵׁנִית֙ (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier), but that run begins at the FOURTH token; the verse's actual opener is וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier) — which I confirm is byte-identical to the openers of MT 10:20 and MT 10:27 and identical at accent-stripped and skeleton tier to the opener of MT 11:10, the very verse this cut separates from. Meanwhile the row's English quote for the same onset, “It will happen in that day that the Lord will set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.” (web:Isa.11.11), DOES include the formula the Hebrew splice excludes, so the two quotations of one onset disagree about where it begins. PRONG 2 (remnant objects): verified against the staged device matrix, which is decisive here. Both verses the row cites carry TWO of the root's four objects, not one: the plain noun the row names, and the survive-verb it does not — אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִשָּׁאֵר֩ (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier) and לִשְׁאָ֣ר עַמּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִשָּׁאֵ֖ר (oshb:Isa.11.16, byte tier), that verb form reaching exactly 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses, MT 11:11 and 11:16, both inside this span), and the matrix independently lists both verses under the verb family. The unnamed object is part of the very noun-plus-relative construction the row treats as its closing echo, so the echo argument runs on an object the row never names. NOT CARRYING: the bare divine name quoted at MT 11:11 belongs to a role-split census, but the row makes no count claim on it, so no count-object naming is owed — an observation, not a defect. NEW FINDING neither primary reports, and machine-confirmed: this row's strongest_rejected_alternative asserts that both halves 'remain governed by the same in-that-day onset with no intervening addressee shift' — a universal claim carrying no adjacent digit-bearing sweep, which the universals check flags. It is one of only two Tier-0 validator flags across all fifteen rows of these two clusters. NEW FINDING: this row sits at high confidence with the frontier flag unset while the sibling row on the other side of the SAME seam holds at medium_low with the flag set and states the boundary is unsettled; two adjacent rows describe one seam with incompatible confidence. VERIFIES: petuchah at MT 11:10 correct type; no petuchah or setumah inside MT 11:11-11:16 (absence never counterevidence); no ketiv/qere in the span; a paseq pair at MT 11:11, single-witness, count-only.
rulings.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field boundary_rationale: either extend the Hebrew splice to the verse's actual opening tokens so the spliced run matches the English quote already given, or stop describing the mid-verse marker as what 'opens' the unit and describe it as what distinguishes the action inside a frame shared with the preceding verse; whichever is chosen, disclose that the opening frame is byte-identical to the openers at web:Isa.10.20 and web:Isa.10.27 and matches web:Isa.11.10 at accent-stripped and skeleton tier, with the tiers named. Field device_notes: name BOTH remnant objects live in web:Isa.11.11 and web:Isa.11.16 — the plain noun and the survive-verb (2 verses, both in this span) — and re-cut the closing-echo argument so it names the object it actually runs on. Field strongest_rejected_alternative: give the no-addressee-shift claim its adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object and unit, or restate it so it carries no universal. Field confidence and frontier_flag_considered: reconcile with the sibling row describing the same seam, or state what this row's own bytes supply that the sibling's do not. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): the Hebrew splice and the English quote for one onset must begin at the same place; every remnant claim names its object before any digit and no two of the four objects are merged or dropped; the universals check returns clean on this row; and no two rows describing one seam carry incompatible confidence without a stated reason.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: the twin-onset recurrence claim holds at no Hebrew tier and is quoted only in English, its form-class gloss misnames the difference between the two speaking verbs, an addressee shift at the hymn's own last verse is contradicted rather than disclosed, and the span's ketiv/qere verse is left unchecked. LF: the Yah-plus-tetragrammaton short-form claim is stated as a categorical 'never blended' without the adjacent digit-bearing count the same device notes correctly supply for the twin-strophe claim beside it.
rulings.grounds: Both primaries hit this row with DISTINCT defects; all the load-bearing prongs verify, so uphold. LF's ITEM, and it is MACHINE-CONFIRMED: device_notes states the short-form stack is 'never blended into the plain tetragrammaton census' — a universal with no adjacent digit-bearing sweep, while the same field two sentences away supplies the sanctioned digit-bearing form for its twin-onset claim. The universals check flags exactly this string; with the sibling flag on the neighbouring row it is one of only two Tier-0 flags across all fifteen rows of these clusters, so LF's own 'low' understates it. OL PRONG 1 (twin-onset recurrence holds at no Hebrew tier): verified by my own re-derivation. MT 12:1 opens וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.12.1, byte tier) and MT 12:4 opens וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֞ם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.12.4, byte tier); I compared them at all three tiers and they differ at byte, accent-stripped AND skeleton. Only the in-that-day core matches, and only at accent-stripped and skeleton tier. So 'restates the same onset formula (sweep: 2 verses)' attaches a digit to a formula identity that holds at no Hebrew tier — the count-object is mis-specified, and the row quotes no Hebrew for either onset. OL PRONG 2 (form-class gloss): verified. וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ (oshb:Isa.12.1, byte tier) and וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֞ם (oshb:Isa.12.4, byte tier) are BOTH second person; only number differs, together with the conjunction vowel — so 'differs in person and number' is a byte-checkable claim the bytes contest. OL PRONG 3 (in-span addressee shift): verified, and I can sharpen it. MT 12:6 opens צַהֲלִ֥י וָרֹ֖נִּי יוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת צִיּ֑וֹן (oshb:Isa.12.6, byte tier), feminine-singular imperatives with a feminine vocative, continued by the second-feminine-singular suffix בְּקִרְבֵּ֖ךְ (oshb:Isa.12.6, byte tier), against the masculine-plural imperatives הוֹד֤וּ לַֽיהוָה֙ קִרְא֣וּ (oshb:Isa.12.4, byte tier) and זַמְּר֣וּ (oshb:Isa.12.5, byte tier); that feminine imperative reaches 3 verses (sweep: 3 verses, MT 10:30, 12:6, 54:1), and it governs a feminine addressee at צַהֲלִ֥י קוֹלֵ֖ךְ בַּת (oshb:Isa.10.30, byte tier). THE SHARPER POINT, which neither primary draws: the number difference OL identifies in prong 2 IS itself an addressee difference between the two strophes — second-person singular at MT 12:1 against second-person plural at MT 12:4 — so the row concedes the byte feature in device_notes while asserting in the same row that both strophes 'share the same speaker, addressee, and doxological register'. The row contradicts itself across two fields, before the further shift at the hymn's last verse is even reached. OL PRONG 4 (ketiv/qere at MT 12:5): the site is real, staged as the doubled pair מידעת מוּדַ֥עַת (oshb:Isa.12.5, byte tier for the spliced pair), and this row is one of only 8 in the whole corpus that leave an in-span ketiv/qere verse undisclosed against 35 that disclose. But the stated rationale is loose: the row's count claim covers MT 12:1 and MT 12:4, not MT 12:5, so nothing sits 'beneath' it, and no unconditional debt is owed — the unconditional symmetry sweep is the petuchah/setumah one. The prong survives on practice, not on obligation, and does not change the verdict because prongs 1-3 are independently sufficient. VERIFIES: the short-form stack יָ֣הּ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.12.2, byte tier) rightly kept as its own count-object, one of exactly 3 sites; petuchah at MT 12:6 correct type; and the closing title קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.12.6, byte tier) cited only in English, where the plene construct reaches 24 verses at skeleton tier against a 25-verse title object — I re-swept and confirm the 24, the difference being the defective spelling outside this stretch.
rulings.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field device_notes: give the 'never blended' sentence its adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object and unit (the short-form sites and the tetragrammaton census are separate count-objects), or restate it without the universal — the universals check must return clean on this row. Field device_notes: replace 'restates the same onset formula (sweep: 2 verses)' with what the bytes carry — the two onsets are distinct at byte, accent-stripped and skeleton tier, and share only the in-that-day core at accent-stripped and skeleton tier — quoting both onsets in Hebrew and naming the tier and the object each digit counts. Field device_notes: correct 'differs in person and number' to differ in NUMBER (both forms are second person), and then reconcile the consequence — since that number difference is an addressee difference, either withdraw the shared-addressee claim in strongest_rejected_alternative or restate the unity ground on register and speaker alone, and disclose the further shift to a feminine-singular addressee at web:Isa.12.6 with its splice and digit (3 verses). Field boundary_evidence_refs or device_notes: disclose the in-span ketiv/qere note at web:Isa.12.5 in the formulation the corpus already attests. Field device_notes: name the closing divine-title object with a pointed splice rather than English alone. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): no recurrence claim survives without the tier at which it holds; no form-class label survives that the pointed bytes contest; no two fields of one row may assert and concede the same feature in opposite directions; and the universals check returns clean.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the formal rejected alternative addresses only the front-seam superscription question and never names the more proximate internal rival, a second hinneh-clause inside this same span; and naming only two precedents while calling a third addition beside them 'a fourth' is an internal count mismatch. OL: keeping the verse-initial burden header with its Babylon oracle is right, but the ground given does not separate this header from the other relative-clause superscription, the span's closing verse is quoted across an undisclosed ketiv/qere note, and the first-person divine voice the back-boundary argument treats as new is already running inside the span.
rulings.grounds: Both primaries hit this row; most items verify, one OL support is REFUTED on the bytes and one LF scope claim needs narrowing, so refine. LF ITEM 1 (internal rival unnamed), upheld with a scope correction: the span does absorb a third-person presentative opening its own sub-scene, הִנֵּ֤ה יוֹם יְהוָה֙ בָּ֔א (oshb:Isa.13.9, byte tier), “Behold, the day of Yahweh comes, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger; to make the land a desolation, and to destroy its sinners out of it.” (web:Isa.13.9), and no rival naming it appears anywhere in the row, while the sibling row treating a structurally parallel presentative at web:Isa.10.33 both discloses it as a live internal-seam candidate and argues why it does not cut. The correction: those two rows belong to DIFFERENT writer parts, so this is a cross-part practice inconsistency rather than one writer treating the same construction two ways within one stretch — real, but a narrower charge than 'this same writing stretch' implies. LF ITEM 2 (internal count mismatch), upheld cleanly: the rejected-alternative calls a stand-alone header row here 'a fourth ... alongside Isa.1.1 and Isa.2.1'. The book carries exactly three headers of this class (MT 1:1, 2:1, 13:1), so setting this one apart would make a THIRD such row, not a fourth; the sentence names two precedents and then miscounts its own addition. OL ITEM 1 (the stated ground does not discriminate), upheld and STRENGTHENED by my own re-derivation: the relative clause אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.13.1, byte tier) is byte-identical not only to MT 2:1's but to MT 1:1's as well — all three headers carry the same accented clause (sweep: 3 verses) — so 'grammatically fused to the content it opens' cannot separate this header from EITHER named precedent. OL's proposed discriminator checks out on the bytes: this header binds its target to the burden-noun in construct, מַשָּׂ֖א בָּבֶ֑ל (oshb:Isa.13.1, byte tier), while the other attaches its target with a preposition after the patronymic, בֶּן אָמ֑וֹץ עַל יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Isa.2.1, byte tier). I also checked OL's digit against its object and it is RIGHT where it could easily have been wrong: the verb-then-prophet adjacency stands at exactly 2 verses (MT 2:1 and 13:1), because MT 1:1 places the name BEFORE the verb — a different object from the 3-verse relative clause. OL ITEM 2, REFUTED AS STATED: the ketiv/qere site at MT 13:16 is real, staged as the doubled pair וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם תשגלנה תִּשָּׁכַֽבְנָה (oshb:Isa.13.16, byte tier for the spliced run), and this row is one of the 8 undisclosed cases corpus-wide against 35 disclosed. But the support offered for it is false about this row: there IS no 'English clause quoted for that boundary' — the row quotes no English at web:Isa.13.16 at all, its only English quotation being the header at web:Isa.13.1. The site survives as a practice deviation; the reason given for it does not.
